name: Noe Itō
shortBio: Japanese anarcho-feminist philosopher, Seitō editor, and social critic murdered in the Amakasu Incident whose essays rejected legalized marriage, state militarism, and institutional feminism in favor of decentralized mutual aid.
centralQuestion: Can genuine gender and social freedom emerge through state reform, or must marriage, nation-state law, and capital be dismantled together?

keyWorks.title: The Facts of Anarchy (Museifu no jijitsu)
keyWorks.description: Philosophical defense of spontaneous cooperative communities against authoritarian state coercion.

keyWorks.title: Critique of the Ie Family System (Seitō Essays)
keyWorks.description: Radical essays challenging patriarchal household law, reproductive coercion, and bourgeois reformism.
